system_prompt:
You are a careful, neutral coder of the REALIZED OUTCOME of a corporate transaction
over the 3-5 years AFTER it closed. You are given ONE evidence slice assembled from
public primary sources (financial filings, reputable press) that describes ONLY the
post-deal trajectory -- how the combined company actually fared. You are
DELIBERATELY NOT shown how the deal was structured at closing (what transferred and
what did not), and you must NOT speculate about the deal's structure. Code STRICTLY
the documented realized outcome. If the slice does not let you determine a field,
you MUST return "uncertain" -- never guess, never infer from outside knowledge.

Emit a single structured record with these fields.

C. FAILURE-PATHWAY INCIDENCE -- code strictly from the DOCUMENTED OUTCOME at the
3-5 year horizon. A pathway is a REALIZED DISRUPTION OVER TIME, not a structural
property of the deal.
  p4_pathway: Is there documented disruption specifically at the product/process
    interface (the acquired product could not be aligned with the operating
    processes over time; product-line/operations incoherence realized after the
    deal)? 1 = yes; 0 = no / none documented; uncertain.
  p5_pathway: Is there documented fracture specifically at the process/organization
    interface (operations vs people/management/culture; integration of operations
    broke against the organization over time)? 1 = yes; 0 = no / none documented;
    uncertain.
  t1_archetype: Is there documented incoherence in the controlling-intent archetype
    itself as it played out (e.g. an announced "merger of equals" that operated as
    one-sided dominance)? A channel SEPARATE from the product/process and
    process/organization pathways. 1 = yes; 0 = no; uncertain.
  t2_model: Is there documented incompatibility of the two business models
    (value-capture logics that could not be reconciled over time)? A channel
    SEPARATE from the pathways above. 1 = yes; 0 = no; uncertain.

D. performance_metric: the single best-documented post-deal outcome scalar in the
   slice (e.g. "divested 80.1% after ~108 months", "~$99bn goodwill write-down",
   "no divestiture; assets retained"). One short phrase. If none, "not documented".

rationale: 2-4 sentences citing the slice lines that drove your p4_pathway and
p5_pathway codes specifically. Cite ONLY realized-outcome evidence; do NOT reason
about how the deal was structured at closing.

Emit ONLY the structured record. Code conservatively: absence of documented
evidence for a pathway is 0 (not-documented); inability to determine is "uncertain".

# Outcome sub-dossier — Alta Mesa Resources, Inc. (formerly Silver Run Acquisition Corporation II) realized record after the business combination

> EVIDENTIARY STANDARD: every factual line ends with a `[SRC: <SEC accession / URL>]`
> tag pointing to a public primary source. A fact that cannot be so sourced is written
> `[UNVERIFIED]` and is never guessed. The fixed outcome window chosen at construction
> was approximately three to five years after the February 9, 2018 closing (i.e.,
> roughly 2021-2023). As documented below, the registrant terminated its SEC reporting
> before that window began, so no public periodic-report record exists for that window
> itself; the realized trajectory that IS publicly documented (through deregistration)
> is reported here instead, per the no-record protocol. This sub-dossier contains no
> information about how the underlying transaction was structured or negotiated.

## Realized financial trajectory through the first full reporting year
- For fiscal year 2018 (the registrant's first full year following the February 9, 2018 closing), the Form 10-K — filed August 27, 2019, several months after its normal due date — reported a net loss for the "Successor" period (February 9-December 31, 2018) of $3,249,347 thousand on a total basis, of which $1,524,699 thousand was attributable to Alta Mesa Resources, Inc. stockholders. [SRC: SEC accession 0001690769-19-000059, Form 10-K FY2018, Consolidated Statements of Operations]
- The FY2018 10-K attributes the loss "mainly to impairment of our proved and unproved oil and gas properties and the long-lived assets, intangible assets and goodwill of our Midstream segment," reporting total impairment of assets of $3,205.1 million, comprising $2,033.7 million in the Upstream segment (unproved properties $742.1 million; proved properties $1,291.6 million) and $1,171.3 million in the Midstream segment (property/equipment $68.4 million; intangible assets $395.0 million; goodwill $692.0 million). [SRC: SEC accession 0001690769-19-000059, Form 10-K FY2018, MD&A / Notes to Financial Statements]
- The same Form 10-K disclosed that current liabilities exceeded current assets by approximately $813.5 million at December 31, 2018, and that management "concluded that these circumstances create substantial doubt regarding our ability to continue as a going concern," citing indebtedness covenants and the prevailing commodity-price environment. [SRC: SEC accession 0001690769-19-000059, Form 10-K FY2018, "Going Concern"]

## Documented events over time
- On September 11, 2019, Alta Mesa Resources, Inc. and certain subsidiaries filed voluntary petitions for reorganization under Chapter 11 of the U.S. Bankruptcy Code in the U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the Southern District of Texas, jointly administered under Case No. 19-35133. [SRC: SEC accession 0001690769-19-000068, Form 8-K Item 1.03]
- On September 13, 2019, Nasdaq notified the company that, as a result of the Chapter 11 filing, its common stock would be removed from listing and registration on Nasdaq; trading was suspended at the opening of business on September 24, 2019, with the company expecting to trade over-the-counter under "AMRQ" and "AMRWWQ." [SRC: SEC accession 0001690769-19-000068, Form 8-K Item 3.01]
- On January 12, 2020, additional subsidiaries — including SRII Opco GP, LLC, SRII Opco, LP, Kingfisher Midstream, LLC, and related Kingfisher entities — also filed Chapter 11 petitions, jointly administered with the September 2019 cases. [SRC: SEC accession 0001690769-20-000006, Form 8-K Item 8.01]
- On December 31, 2019, subsidiaries entered two Purchase and Sale Agreements with a single buyer, BCE-Mach III LLC: the Kingfisher assets (gathering systems, pipelines, compressor stations and related facilities) for total cash consideration of $85,250,000, and substantially all of the Alta Mesa upstream assets (wells, leases and related equipment) for total cash consideration of $224,750,000 — combined cash consideration of $310,000,000, implemented through the Chapter 11 proceedings and contingent on Bankruptcy Court approval. [SRC: SEC accession 0001690769-20-000003, Form 8-K Item 1.01]
- On January 24, 2020, the Bankruptcy Court approved execution of both purchase and sale agreements ("the Bankruptcy Sales"), with closing expected in February 2020. [SRC: SEC accession 0001690769-20-000027, Form 15-12B]
- On February 13 and February 19, 2020, the registrant filed Forms 15-12G and 15-12B terminating/suspending its duty to file reports under the Securities Exchange Act, reporting approximately 66 holders of record of its warrants at that time. [SRC: SEC accession 0001690769-20-000027, Form 15-12B]

## Post-deregistration public-record status (feasibility-relevant)
- No Form 10-K or other periodic report has been located from the registrant (CIK 1690769) after the February 2020 Form 15 filings. [SRC: SEC accession 0001690769-20-000027, Form 15-12B]
- A search of SEC EDGAR for the buyer entity and its affiliates (BCE-Mach Holdings LLC, CIK 0001734054; BCE-Mach Holdings II LLC, CIK 0001791673; BCE-Mach Holdings III LLC, CIK 0001799974) shows only Form D exempt-securities-offering notices on file for those entities — no Form 10-K, 10-Q, or other periodic annual/quarterly report — indicating the acquired businesses did not continue as a separate SEC-reporting entity after the 2020 asset sales. [SRC: https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&company=BCE-Mach&type=&dateb=&owner=include&count=40&output=atom]
- Consequently, for the fixed ~2021-2023 outcome window, there is no public periodic-report record of the acquired businesses' post-February-2020 financial or operating trajectory; this portion of the outcome is coded **uncertain (no public record)** rather than inferred from any private buyer's non-public results. [UNVERIFIED]

## Outcome summary (realized record only)
- The registrant's first full post-closing fiscal year (2018) produced a reported net loss of approximately $3.2 billion, driven primarily by $3,205.1 million of combined upstream and midstream asset/intangible/goodwill impairments, alongside a disclosed going-concern qualification. Roughly nineteen months after closing the registrant and its subsidiaries entered Chapter 11 proceedings and were removed from Nasdaq listing; substantially all operating assets (both the upstream and midstream businesses) were subsequently sold in bankruptcy to a single private buyer for combined cash consideration of $310 million, and the registrant terminated its SEC registration in February 2020. No public periodic-report record of the underlying businesses exists for the remainder of the originally fixed 3-5-year outcome window. [SRC: SEC accession 0001690769-19-000059, Form 10-K FY2018] [SRC: SEC accession 0001690769-19-000068, Form 8-K] [SRC: SEC accession 0001690769-20-000003, Form 8-K] [SRC: SEC accession 0001690769-20-000027, Form 15-12B]

[SLICE END]

Roughly nineteen months after closing the registrant and its subsidiaries entered Chapter 11 proceedings and were removed from Nasdaq listing; substantially all operating assets (both the upstream and midstream businesses) were subsequently sold in bankruptcy to a single private buyer for combined cash consideration of $310 million, and the registrant terminated its SEC registration in February 2020. No public periodic-report record of the underlying businesses exists for the remainder of the originally fixed 3-5-year outcome window.
